observations:
Torah #82 is a short, tightly focused teaching. The source text (18 lines) addresses a single conceptual axis: the relationship between holy silence (שתיקה), circumcision (מילה), the intermediate domain (נגה/חשמ"ל), the divine flame (שלהבת י"ה), and the three impure klipot (ערלה/שלש קלפות). All bechina-connected concepts fall cleanly into the five existing packages (three good, one evil, one neutral). No independent conceptual domain with 3+ bechina-linked concepts emerges from the source text that is not already covered.

The following additional concepts appear in the text but do not form a new independent package:

1. 'הנעלבים ואינם עולבים' / 'שומעים חרפתם ואינם משיבים' / 'עושין מאהבה' — These are behavioral descriptions (the people who practice holy silence). They are not a new conceptual domain; they are the practical embodiment of Package 5 (שתיקה) flowing into Package 2 (נגה absorbed into kedusha). They could be added as eitza nodes to the existing packages but do not constitute an independent bechina domain.

2. 'שלש שני ערלה' / 'רבעי' — These are agricultural/halakhic references used as metaphors. שלש שני ערלה is already captured by Package 4 (= three klipot), and רבעי is already captured by Package 2 (= נגה). No new package.

3. 'נשמת העשוקים' — While this is an interesting concept (the soul of the oppressed as an aspect of נגה), it is identified in the text as a bechina of נגה, placing it within Package 2, not forming an independent domain.

4. The Gemara quote frame (Shabbat 88b) — 'הנעלבים ואינם עולבים... עליהם הכתוב אומר' — is structural framework, not conceptual content forming a new domain.

The teaching's conceptual structure is complete with five packages. The eitza connections (which are not used for packages) show the causal flow: קדשת הברית/מילה/יוסף →[eitza]→ gathering of the klipot (their power is nullified); שלהבת י"ה →[eitza]→ protection of holiness from klipot on Shabbat eve. These causal flows connect the packages but do not generate new package domains.
